Issued at 234 PM EDT Wed Jul 22 2026

Currently-Tonight...East coast sea breeze will continue to shift 
inland, with isolated to scattered showers and storms still possible 
along this boundary. However, greatest potential for rain (up to 30-
40%) will exist across areas south of Orlando through the afternoon 
and with the sea breeze collision across Lake County into this 
evening (from 8-10 PM). Dry air aloft may allow for an isolated 
stronger storm or two, mainly from the sea breeze collision, 
producing frequent lightning, strong wind gusts up to 40-50 mph and 
locally heavy rainfall of 1-3 inches. Convection will then
diminish, with mostly dry conditions then forecast overnight. 
However, low level onshore flow may again lead to a few onshore 
moving showers along the Treasure Coast late in the night through 
early morning Thursday (chance of rain 20%). Warm and muggy 
conditions will exist overnight, with lows in the mid to upper 70s
for many locations. 

Thursday-Friday...TS Bertha is forecast to continue a westward 
movement along the northern Gulf coast through Thursday, before 
weakening into a Tropical Depression as it continues farther inland 
into TX on Friday. As this system continues west, a broad ridge 
aloft will persist across Florida through late week. At the surface 
the Atlantic ridge axis will remain extended near to north of the 
area, leading to a predominant onshore flow. Drier airmass (PW 
values 1.5-1.6 inches) and easterly flow on Thursday will keep 
rain chances limited (10-20%) and focused mostly inland and toward
west central Florida. Moisture then increases into Friday as a 
weak inverted sfc trough approaches and moves westward across the 
region, increasing PW values to 2+ inches. This will lead to a 
rise in shower and storms chances, with scattered to locally 
numerous showers and storms developing into the afternoon and 
shifting westward through the early evening. Rain chances increase
to 30-60% for much of the region, with greatest coverage focused 
near to south of Orlando. North of Sanford, showers and storms may
remain more isolated (PoPs 10-20%). Lingering pockets of drier 
air may still allow for a few stronger storms into Friday, with 
gusty winds, frequent lightning and locally heavy downpours 
continuing to be the main threats. 

It will remain hot and humid into late week, with highs in the low 
to mid 90s. There will be little relief on Thursday as rain chances 
remain limited, and highs for inland areas are forecast within 1-2 
degrees of record highs. Could also see some upper 90s in spots near 
to northwest of I-4 tomorrow afternoon. Peak heat index values look 
to remain below Heat Advisory thresholds, ranging from 100-107F, as 
drier air will mix down to lower dewpoints tomorrow, and even with 
the added humidity Friday, the increase in showers and storms should 
bring some heat relief into the afternoon. Still, a moderate to 
major HeatRisk will still lead to dangerous heat impacts into late 
week. 

Saturday-Tuesday...(Modified Previous Discussion) Upper level high 
pressure over the Plains and the Deep South will remain in place as 
a trough over the Midwest shifts eastward towards the Atlantic coast 
and digs southward towards the Florida into the weekend and early 
next week. At the surface, the Atlantic high pressure ridge axis 
will shift southward through the weekend as a low pressure system 
pushes off the coast of the Carolinas. An associated frontal 
boundary will dig through the Deep South into late week and into 
northern Florida before stalling over the weekend. The front will 
then drift slowly southward into early next week as it weakens. 
Moisture will continue to increase across the area this weekend, 
with shower and lightning storm activity primarily being driven by 
sea breeze interactions/collisions. Offshore (westerly) flow will 
also return this weekend and continue into early next week, which 
will favor higher coverage of storms across the eastern side of the 
peninsula near the coast, with shower and storm chances remaining 
near to above normal. Any lingering showers and storms will diminish 
each evening through the overnight hours. However, isolated to 
scattered showers will remain possible across the Atlantic waters 
each night.

A slight warming trend is forecast through the weekend, with above 
normal temperatures forecast through Sunday. Current guidance 
indicates that increasing cloud coverage and rain chances will help 
keep temperatures closer to normal Monday and Tuesday. Peak heat 
indices will generally be 100-107F, with some locations potentially 
nearing Heat Advisory criteria, especially over the weekend. 
Confidence in this remains low however, so will continue to monitor. 
Lows will generally be in the 70s each night.
